summary: 28-year-old woman with a witnessed 2-minute generalised tonic-clonic seizure, tongue bite and incontinence, now fully recovered; glucose, sodium and calcium normal.

inputs.hpi: Colleagues saw her go stiff and then shake all four limbs for about 2 minutes at her desk 90 minutes ago; bitten tongue, wet herself, confused for 20 minutes afterwards. Now back to normal. No previous episodes, no alcohol or drugs, no head injury. Drives to work.

exam.general: Alert, orientated. Lateral tongue bite. Pulse 82/min regular, BP 124/76, temperature 36.9°C.

inputs.socialHistory: Accountant. Drives. No alcohol excess, no drugs.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: First unprovoked generalised tonic-clonic seizure
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: First generalised tonic-clonic seizure, recovered: ECG, bloods, first-seizure specialist referral within 2 weeks, driving and safety advice.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no node for this condition (surgical diseases only); top 3 cholecystitis, appendicitis, GORD. Symptom inference ranks epilepsy/seizure #1.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add medical-emergency diseases to lib/pane-engine (or a separate medical-mimic layer) driven by labs/vitals/chips, or show the symptom-inference leader beside the PANE top 3 when PANE has no matching node.

mustInclude.note: NICE NG217: 12-lead ECG in adults with a suspected seizure (cardiac causes). Graded as management because the web prompts add ECGs as plan lines.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No ECG (the pre-operative ECG prompt is age ≥40 only).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a first-seizure prompt: ECG, glucose, first-seizure clinic within 2 weeks, driving/safety advice (NICE NG217).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No neurology / first-seizure referral; only two cervical-screening lines in management.

mustInclude.note: Driving and safety advice is a patient- and public-safety item.

mustExclude.note: Antiseizure medicine is a specialist decision after a first seizure; valproate in a woman of childbearing potential needs particular care.

guideline.name: NICE NG217 — Epilepsies in children, young people and adults
guideline.section: After a first suspected seizure: urgent referral to a specialist (seen within 2 weeks); 12-lead ECG in adults; blood glucose; advice on driving and safety (DVLA), and on what to do if another seizure happens; status epilepticus: benzodiazepine (buccal midazolam or IV lorazepam)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Epilepsies in children, young people and adults. NICE guideline NG217. London: NICE; 2022.

rationale: NICE NG217: ECG, specialist referral within 2 weeks, driving and safety advice.
